attempts.label: DANDI:000249
attempts.paper_title: Innate and plastic mechanisms for maternal behaviour in auditory cortex
attempts.entry_title: Maternal behaviour and temporal tuning in auditory cortex (Schiavo et al. 2020)
attempts.summary: Here is the paragraph for that file: None of the paper's main findings could be confirmed or refuted in this data. The imaging findings, such as broader tuning in experienced females, could not be tested because the dandiset holds only raw movies, with no cell regions or record of which call played on each trial. The retrieval behaviour findings are in neither the dandiset nor its linked collection. In the whole-cell recordings the current almost never follows the calls (2 of 39 cells), so the excitation and inhibition findings could not be tested. Among minor findings, oxytocin enhancing spiking held under an assumed comparison, and faster IPSC depression in slices did not.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Schiavo, Valtcheva, Bair-Marshall, Song, Martin and Froemke (2020) on dandiset 000249, which holds the raw two-photon movies of 54 mice, and on the figshare collection the dandiset links, which holds the in vivo and slice whole-cell recordings and the operant touch times. The movies carry no ROIs, stimulus times or stimulus order, so the imaging findings cannot be tested; the whole-cell, slice and operant findings are tested on the figshare recordings.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Schiavo et al. (2020) from dandiset 000249 and its figshare recordings

outcomes.notes: Every subject has a figshare item titled with its mouse id (54 of 54), and the titles agree with the NWB experiment descriptions on experience group (49 of 49 where the description gives one), cell class (54 of 54) and right hemisphere (54 of 54). The five tones-only mice take their group from the titles, which the criterion allows: EV56 and EV62 experienced (their descriptions call them NV56 and NV62), NV64, NV66 and NV140 naive. Counts match the paper for EV excitatory left (9), EV interneurons (5), EV right cortex (4), dam (1), CH+575 (6), CH+575 opto-OT (4) and NV interneurons (6). 14 subjects have a first retrieval session against the paper's 13 chronic virgins, and 23 naive excitatory mice of several kinds (9 chronic, 5 non-cohoused controls, 6 CH+575, 3 tones only) stand against the 12 of Fig. 1f, which the paper does not name. No file has a stimulus series or trial table, so no presentation can be assigned its call or ISI, which makes the result partial under the criterion. Folding the movies finds the trial period (40 frames, 10.24 s), and in 31 of 38 three-call movies a cycle of three trials, but not which call each trial played.
deviations: Groups are read from the NWB experiment descriptions and, where these give none, from the figshare item titles of the same mouse id (collection doi:10.6084/m9.figshare.c.5043830.v6), as the criterion allows.

The dandiset's NWB files hold only raw, unaligned two-photon movies. They have no ROIs or fluorescence traces (the paper drew ROIs by hand), no stimulus series, no trial table and no times of the calls; the session description names the three to five calls or morphs of a recording but not the order in which they were played (pseudorandom, Methods). Folding the movies recovers the trial period (40 frames, 10.24 s), and in 31 of 38 three-call movies a cycle of three trials, but nothing says which call is played at which position of the cycle (data check). Responses cannot be assigned to named calls, so the claim cannot be tested. The figshare imaging items hold the same movies as TIFF files with the same descriptions.

It needs the ISI distribution of Fig. 1a (fig1a-isi-distribution, blocked as data missing) and call-evoked dF/F per ISI, which the movies cannot give without stimulus times and order (metadata insufficient, as for the other imaging claims).

The start of cohousing is not recorded in the files or the metadata, so the hours to retrieval onset cannot be measured. 14 subjects have a session named first retrieval (the paper has 13). The hours from the last session imaged before it (base, 24hrsPRE or 48HrsPRE) are 23.9 to 52.1, and from the last session named base 23.9 to 144.9 (NV50 has only a 24hrsPRE session), but either bounds onset only if cohousing began after that session, which nothing states; they decide nothing.

At 175 ms (14 EPSC and 13 IPSC cells) IPSCs do not depress more than EPSCs. Per trial, mean Sn/S1 over pulses 2 to 5 is 0.90 (IPSC) against 0.68 (EPSC), p = 0.33, and no pulse differs after Bonferroni (adjusted p 1.0). On per-file mean traces, 0.57 against 0.65, p = 0.39; pulses 2 and 3 adjusted p 0.15 and 0.06. 75 ms does not differ (p 0.52 and 0.72). At 575 ms the unpaired tests do not differ (p 0.82 and 0.08), but on mean traces a paired test finds IPSCs lower (0.55 against 0.66, p = 0.022). Per-trial IPSC ratios are noisy; 35 trials with no first response above baseline were dropped and 17 cell means fall outside 0 to 2. The pulse times read from the protocol fall on the stimulus artefacts (steepest current change a median 0.5 ms after the computed time, within 1 ms for 91.8% of 740 pulses). At 175 ms the per-trial and mean-trace IPSC ratios move in opposite directions (0.90 and 0.57 against 0.68 and 0.65), neither significantly.
deviations: Assumed: the peak is the largest inward (EPSC) or outward (IPSC) current 2 to 30 ms after each pulse (to 2 ms before the next pulse at 50 ms periods) against the mean of the 5 ms before it. The Methods say only "peak amplitude ... normalized to the event evoked by the first stimulation on each trial"; local baselines are the usual choice for trains.
Trials with a first response not above baseline give no ratio and are dropped; the mean trace per file is shown as a variant.
One-way ANOVA with two groups is run as the equivalent unpaired t-test; a paired test is shown as a variant.
12 of the 13 cells at 575 ms; file 19o11005 (Cell 20) is listed but not on figshare.
The 75 ms bin includes trains at 50 ms periods, at the edge of the Methods' 75 plus or minus 25 ms.

outcomes.notes: The readings disagree, and the criterion blocks the claim then. Prototypes increase mean press duration under all four (session 1 against 8, p = 0.025 with the median-interval gap and 0.0076 with the 100 ms gap; sessions 1-2 against 7-8, p = 0.032 and 0.021). Fast and slow are not significant under three readings (p 0.081 to 0.73), but with the 100 ms gap and session 1 against 8 slow increases (p = 0.040) and fast reaches p = 0.050. The reading closest to the paper's p-values (0.03, 0.24, 0.13) is the median-interval gap with session 1 against 8 (0.025, 0.081, 0.17). For the paper's authors, which gap ends a press and which sessions were compared. The gap that ends a press under the median-interval rule grows with time in the session (1.5 ms before 100 s, 15 ms to 1000 s, 150 ms after), because a gap must exceed one and a half printed steps.
deviations: Touch times are printed with five significant digits, so a press can be resolved only to 0.1 ms below 10 s, 1 ms below 100 s, 10 ms to 1000 s and 100 ms after; a gap must exceed one and a half local steps (1 ms taken as the step below 100 s) to end a press, under both gap readings, so the median-interval rule ends a press at 1.5, 15 or 150 ms depending on when it falls.

The median inter-sample interval (reading a) is the polling period of the task code, taken once, pooled over sessions, from the times printed at 0.1 ms (below 10 s), 0.70 ms; above 10 s the printed intervals are quantized at 1 ms or more. Before revision a mean over the 1 ms part was used (about 0.7 ms); the outcome is unchanged.
Two mice miss one session each (NV24 session 5, NV38 session 3); neither is a compared session.

outcomes.notes: In the deposited in vivo recordings the current almost never follows the calls, so the claim cannot be tested on the cells it is about. The Methods' evoked measure is in the expected direction at p < 0.05 in 2 of 39 cell recordings, against 3 of 39 for the same measure before the call; no cell has a mean response 0-300 ms after onset at p < 0.05 (mean over cells 0.25 pA for EPSCs); 13 of 110 files have a sweep-locked deflection 0-3 s after onset at p < 0.05, more than the 5.5 expected by chance (binomial p = 0.0034), but only 3 of them, from two cells (naive 190326_e1, both EPSC files, and experienced 190313_e2, one of two), carry a current in the expected direction during the call, first exceeding the null 0.39 to 0.51 s after onset and peaking at 37 to 48 pA; the other 10 peak at scattered times, 9 against the expected direction; and the inclusion rule keeps 1 of 39 (2 s.d., cell 190326_e1) or none (3 s.d.). As computed on every listed cell it would not be reproduced: naive prototype-evoked EPSCs (20.0 pA, largest 5 trials) are not larger than morph-evoked ones (17.4, 18.3, 16.2 pA; adjusted p 0.12, 0.94, 0.20; RM ANOVA p = 0.18), and no variant gives p < 0.05 for all three; experienced EPSCs are not correlated with ISI (r = -0.14, p = 0.35; -0.09 to -0.21 under every variant). No experienced pair differs (smallest adjusted p 0.30 to 1.0) and the naive correlation is not significant (r = -0.07, p = 0.61).
deviations: Call onset, offset and ISI come from the recorded microphone channel. The onset is the start of the sound (envelope above its median by 6 robust s.d.); before revision it was the first loud syllable, which came a median 193 ms (up to 644 ms) late because the first syllable of many calls is quiet, and that rule is run as a variant. In 82 of 83 morph-set files the four call durations form four groups in a fixed order (prototype, 125, 275, 575 ms), and the ISI is assigned by duration rank; one two-sweep file uses the nearest bin of the measured gap. The sets hold the legends' ISIs, not the Methods' 125, 225 and 575 ms.

Assumed, for the Methods' inclusion rule ("Only neurons that exhibited at least five significant prototype-evoked E/IPSCs"), which does not define a significant PSC: a trial whose evoked current in the expected direction exceeds k s.d. of the cell's sham measure (k = 2 and 3). It keeps 1 of 39 cell recordings at k = 2 and none at k = 3; the other checks of the data check, which need no such definition, agree that the currents almost never follow the calls (two cells carry an inward current during the call).

Every listed cell is used for the computed values; 12 experienced and 14 naive EPSC cells as in the paper, and 7 experienced (paper 6) and 6 naive IPSC cells. One experienced IPSC cell (190410_e1) has 4 or 5 trials per ISI.
The largest 5 or 10 trials are ranked by absolute value (the Methods' "absolute magnitudes"), and, as a second reading, by the current in the expected direction.

The spreadsheet notes are applied (stop or drop at a sweep keeps the sweeps before it, from sweep N keeps the later ones, drop or block + stop drops the file), only the best call's set is used where a note names one, and sweeps whose holding current contradicts the listed potential are dropped (file 19424013 is listed at -70 mV but carries +560 pA). Using every sweep is a variant.
Experienced cells pool dams and EVs; the spreadsheets do not say which are which.
One listed file (193260007, an IPSC file of naive cell 190326_e1) is not on figshare; the cell's other IPSC file is used.
The Bonferroni family is read as the three comparisons with the prototype that the legend reports; all six pairs are shown.

As computed it would not be reproduced: experienced EPSCs exceed naive ones at 125, 275 and 575 ms (one-tailed p 0.0023, 0.0062, 0.0047) but also at the prototype (33.5 against 20.0 pA, p = 0.013; 0.0051 to 0.041 under every variant). The same measure before the call shows the same difference (EV 32.0 to 35.7 against NV 14.8 to 19.6 pA, one-tailed p 0.0002 to 0.0047), and the baseline s.d. is 11.4 pA in experienced and 5.3 pA in naive recordings.

outcomes.notes: The experienced in vivo whole-cell article (figshare 12611657 v3) lists 12 cells by date and number, with no field saying which 4 come from dams and which 8 from experienced virgins, and the ABF files carry no subject information.

In 9 oxytocin cells spike probability rises from 0.035-0.051 to 0.48-0.56 15 to 30 minutes after wash onset (Friedman chi2 = 51.35, p = 6e-08). Dunn's comparisons, Bonferroni over the five stimuli, give stimuli 2 to 5 adjusted p 0.022, 0.014, 0.0011, 0.020 and stimulus 1 p = 0.071 (paper 0.009, 0.008, 0.001, 0.04 and 0.34), although stimulus 1 also rises (0.044 to 0.48). 5 ACSF controls show no change (Friedman p = 0.56, adjusted p >= 0.79); counting the control window from the first baseline sweep brings in all 7, again with no change (Friedman p = 0.39, adjusted p >= 0.47). Over all 45 pairs only stimulus 4 is significant (p = 0.0098), and Wilcoxon tests find stimulus 1 significant as well (p = 0.0078), so the outcome rests on the comparison family.
deviations: Assumed: the Friedman test runs over ten columns (baseline and post for each of five stimuli), with Dunn's comparisons of baseline against post for each stimulus, Bonferroni over five; the legend gives one p per stimulus, which fits five planned comparisons. All 45 pairs and Wilcoxon tests are variants and change the outcome.
A spike is a crossing of 0 mV between a pulse and the next, a standard choice.

Baseline is the files the spreadsheet labels baseline or PRE (the first file for one control cell with no such label; the notebook prints each file's label and role); for controls the 15 to 30 minute window starts at the first sweep after the baseline files, a reading of "following baseline acquisition", and from the first baseline sweep as a variant.

Under the main reading two of the 7 controls (191202B, 191202C) have no sweeps in the window: each has one 60-sweep baseline file (0 to 11.8 min) and one later file ending 19.3 and 24.8 min after the first baseline sweep.

findings.statement: The NWB files hold only raw, unaligned two-photon movies. There are no ROIs or fluorescence traces, no stimulus times, no trial tables and no record of which call each trial played (pseudorandom order, Methods), so none of the paper's 20 imaging findings can be tested from the dandiset. The figshare imaging items hold the same movies.

The behavioural data of Figs. 1c, 4c-e and Extended Data Figs. 2 and 8-9 (pup retrieval, latencies, y-maze) and the vocalization recordings of Fig. 1a are in neither the dandiset nor the figshare collection it links. The paper's figshare DOI 10.35092/yhjc.c.5037737 does not resolve.

Groups (experienced or naive, dam, CH+575, opto-OT, cell type, hemisphere) are given only in free-text experiment descriptions; the indicator and location fields are "unknown" in every file, and the start of cohousing, needed for retrieval onset, is not recorded.
Three recordings (sessions of 2018-03-08 named plus24hrs_postexp1) are deposited under both sub-NV58 and sub-NV63, with the same start times and frames; nothing says to which mouse they belong.

Subjects EV56 and EV62 are described as NV56 and NV62 in their own experiment descriptions, and the five tones-only mice carry no experience group in theirs; the figshare item titles give it (EV56_Experienced_Exc and so on).
The in vivo whole-cell spreadsheet of experienced females does not say which cells come from dams, so the dams-against-EVs comparison of Extended Data Fig. 6g,h cannot be made.
In the in vivo whole-cell article of experienced females, file 19424013 is listed at -70 mV but carries about +560 pA throughout, as at a depolarized holding potential.
Files listed in the figshare spreadsheets but not deposited, 193260007 (naive in vivo, listed number with an extra digit) and 19o11005 (slice, Cell 20 at 575 ms).

The operant touch-time csv files print times with five significant digits, so after 1000 s of a session they step by 0.1 s and 99% of samples repeat the previous value; press durations can be resolved only to that step.

The Methods give the in vivo morph set as ISIs of 125, 225 and 575 ms; the microphone channel of the recordings shows 125, 275 and 575 ms with the prototype, as the figure legends say, played in a fixed order, not pseudorandom.

In the in vivo whole-cell recordings the current almost never follows the played calls: the evoked measure is in the expected direction at p < 0.05 in 2 of 39 cell recordings (3 of 39 before the call), no cell responds 0-300 ms after onset, 13 of 110 files have a sweep-locked deflection (5.5 expected by chance) of which 3, from two cells (190326_e1 and 190313_e2), carry an inward current during the call from about 0.4 s after onset, and the Methods' inclusion rule keeps at most 1 of 39. The experienced recordings are about twice as noisy as the naive ones (baseline s.d. 11.4 against 5.3 pA), and the largest-trial measure gives the same experienced-naive difference before the call as during it.

For the paper's authors (fig1i-operant-prototypes, ed5b-press-count-unchanged), which gap between touch samples ends a lever press, and whether session 1 was compared with session 8 or the first with the last sessions. The readings give different outcomes for the fast and slow groups.

For the paper's authors (the in vivo claims and ed9b-oxytocin-enhances-spiking), how a significant PSC was defined for the inclusion rule, how many of the "largest 5-10 evoked trials" were averaged per cell and whether they were ranked by absolute value, and the Dunn comparison family of Extended Data Fig. 9b.

The imaging Methods say the calls were played in a pseudorandom order at 0.1 Hz. The movies recur every 40 frames (10.24 s, 0.098 Hz) and the tone files every 20 frames (5.12 s); in 31 of 38 three-call movies (one per subject) folding at three trial periods stands above two and four, as a fixed cycle of three calls would. No file says which call is played at which position of the cycle.
The first syllable of many played calls is much quieter than the rest on the microphone channel of the in vivo recordings; an onset taken at the first loud syllable comes a median 193 ms late.

disagreements.reason: As computed it would be not reproduced, but the notebook's own control shows the measure picks up no call-evoked current: only 1 of 12 EV and 2 of 14 NV EPSC cells and 1 of 7 and 0 of 6 IPSC cells show a call-evoked current of the expected sign, about the rate the sham window gives, 46-48% of trials have the expected sign, and the Methods say every analysed cell had at least five significant prototype-evoked PSCs. The notebook never shows a trial-averaged current aligned to the microphone onset. EV has 7 IPSC cells against 6, and the inclusion rule is not applied.

As computed it would be not reproduced, because the prototype comparison is significant in every variant. The pre-call sham measure shows the same EV>NV differences, so what is being measured is recording noise, not evoked EPSCs. Trials are ranked by absolute value, so wrong-sign noise trials get selected; the largest trials in the expected direction were not run, and with EV baseline noise about twice NV's the top-k magnitudes favour EV whatever the response.
The 5- and 10-trial readings disagree at 175 ms. In any case the sham IPSC shows the same EV>NV difference, and EV has 7 IPSC cells against the paper's 6.
As computed it would be not reproduced (EV r about 0.06-0.09, p about 0.7, against 0.47). It rests on the same unvalidated measure, with 7 cells, not 6.
As computed it would be not reproduced: the paired p at 575 ms is 0.17-0.48. Same caveat as ed6ef.

entries.name: 000249-schiavo-2020
entries.title: Maternal behaviour and temporal tuning in auditory cortex (Schiavo et al. 2020)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Schiavo, Valtcheva, Bair-Marshall, Song, Martin and Froemke (2020) on dandiset 000249, which holds the raw two-photon movies of 54 mice, and on the figshare collection the dandiset links, which holds the in vivo and slice whole-cell recordings and the operant touch times. The movies carry no ROIs, stimulus times or stimulus order, so the imaging findings cannot be tested; the whole-cell, slice and operant findings are tested on the figshare recordings.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Schiavo et al. (2020) from dandiset 000249 and its figshare recordings
